canonical_algorithm.paper: M. Torquati, Single-Producer/Single-Consumer Queues on Shared Cache Multi-Core Systems

official_artifact.current_project_license_statement: dual LGPL-3.0/MIT for current releases; not mapped to the exact 2010 artifact

semantic_adaptations: Independent C++20 std::atomic pointer mapping of the protocol-fixed algorithm
Cache-line separation takes an explicit verified runtime byte count instead of a compiled platform guess
Null payload construction is rejected before queue operation
No software-prefetch package site is implemented in Stage 5
memory_order_mapping: producer acquire-loads a slot before reuse and release-stores an accepted pointer
consumer acquire-loads a published pointer and release-stores null before reuse
producer and consumer modulo cursors are non-atomic single-writer state

atomic_and_alignment.alignment_expectation: natural atomic alignment; slot array and ownership states use explicit verified cache-line base alignment

claim_boundary.linearizability: bounded FIFO try operations for exactly one producer and one consumer
claim_boundary.wait_free: each individual try operation under valid SPSC and lock-free pointer-atomic preconditions
claim_boundary.lock_free: no claim beyond the same reviewed SPSC try-operation object
claim_boundary.excluded: MPSC, MPMC, nullable payloads, retries, waits, allocation, software-prefetch packages, measurement
